test_cases.test_name: CSV Import and X-bar/R Chart Creation with Nelson Rules
test_cases.objective: Verify the system can import CSV data, create X-bar/R control charts, and correctly apply vendor-standard Nelson rules for statistical process control.
prerequisites: Test CSV file with 100k data points
Valid user credentials with chart creation permissions
SPC dashboard installed and configured

test_steps.action: Log into the SPC dashboard using valid credentials with appropriate permissions
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and accesses the main dashboard interface

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section and select CSV import option
test_steps.expected_result: CSV import interface loads with file selection and configuration options

test_steps.action: Upload the test CSV file containing 100k data points and configure data mapping
test_steps.expected_result: System processes the CSV file within 5 seconds and displays data mapping confirmation

test_steps.action: Create an X-bar/R chart using the imported data with Nelson rules enabled
test_steps.expected_result: Chart renders within 2 seconds with all Nelson rules correctly applied and visible

acceptance_criteria: CSV import completes within 5 seconds
X-bar/R chart renders within 2 seconds
All vendor-standard Nelson rules are correctly applied and visible
Statistical calculations match expected values
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 electronic records requirements
GAMP 5 Category 3 software validation guidelines
data_integrity_requirements: Data integrity maintained during CSV import process
Statistical calculations preserve original data accuracy
Chart configurations stored as controlled records

test_cases.test_name: Role-Based Access Control and Export Functionality Verification
test_cases.objective: Validate that role-based access control functions correctly and export features (PDF/CSV) work as specified for different user roles.
prerequisites: Multiple user accounts with different role permissions
Pre-configured chart with released dataset
Email server configured for scheduled reports

test_steps.action: Log in as a user with administrator role and create a chart with a dataset
test_steps.expected_result: Administrator can create charts and access all functionality without restrictions

test_steps.action: Release the dataset and verify it becomes read-only for all users
test_steps.expected_result: Released dataset is marked as read-only and cannot be modified by any user

test_steps.action: Log in as a viewer role user and attempt to access the released chart
test_steps.expected_result: Viewer can access the chart in read-only mode but cannot make modifications

test_steps.action: Export the chart to PDF and CSV formats using standard vendor export features
test_steps.expected_result: Exports complete successfully with all data preserved and formatted correctly

test_steps.action: Schedule a report email using the vendor scheduler for the exported chart
test_steps.expected_result: Report email is scheduled successfully and confirmation is provided

acceptance_criteria: Role-based access controls enforce appropriate permissions
Released datasets are read-only for all users
PDF and CSV exports preserve all data accurately
Scheduled email reports are configured correctly
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 access controls
Data integrity and security requirements
Electronic record retention policies
data_integrity_requirements: Data integrity maintained during export processes
Access controls prevent unauthorized data modification
Audit trail records access and export activities

test_cases.objective: Verify that the system can successfully schedule and send automated report emails using the vendor's built-in scheduler functionality.
prerequisites: System installed and configured
Valid user account with scheduling permissions
Email server configured in system
Test dataset available
Email test account configured

test_steps.action: Log into the system with a user account that has scheduling permissions
test_steps.expected_result: User successfully logs in and gains access to the scheduling functionality

test_steps.action: Navigate to the report scheduling section and configure a new scheduled report with PDF export format
test_steps.expected_result: System allows creation of scheduled report with all required parameters configured

test_steps.action: Set the schedule to run immediately or within a short test timeframe and save the configuration
test_steps.expected_result: System accepts the schedule configuration and confirms successful save

test_steps.action: Monitor the email test account for the scheduled report delivery within the expected timeframe
test_steps.expected_result: Email is received with the attached PDF report as scheduled

acceptance_criteria: Scheduled reports are successfully generated and emailed according to configured schedule
PDF attachments contain correct report data
System provides confirmation of successful scheduling
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 compliance for automated processes
GAMP 5 guidelines for configured software validation
data_integrity_requirements: Scheduled reports must maintain data accuracy and completeness
Email delivery must be reliable and consistent
Report content must match source data
urs_requirements: URS-020-006: The system shall support scheduled report emails using vendor scheduler
related_tests: OQ-001: CSV Import and X-bar/R Chart Creation

test_cases.test_name: Large Dataset Performance and Chart Rendering Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that the system meets performance requirements for loading large datasets and rendering charts within specified timeframes on supported hardware.
prerequisites: System installed on supported hardware
Test dataset with 100k+ data points
Performance monitoring tools available
System baseline established

test_steps.action: Prepare a CSV test file containing exactly 100,000 data points in the system's required format
test_steps.expected_result: Test file is created with correct format and exact data point count

test_steps.action: Initiate the import process and start timing the operation using a stopwatch or system timer
test_steps.expected_result: Import process begins immediately and system indicates progress

test_steps.action: Record the time when the import completes and data becomes available for chart creation
test_steps.expected_result: Data import completes successfully within 5 seconds as specified in requirements

test_steps.action: Apply filter changes to the dataset and time the chart re-rendering process
test_steps.expected_result: Charts re-render completely within 2 seconds after filter application

acceptance_criteria: 100k data points load in less than 5 seconds
Charts render completely within 2 seconds after filter changes
System remains responsive during high-load operations
No data corruption or loss during processing
regulatory_basis: FDA guidance on computerized systems performance
GAMP 5 Category 3 software performance validation requirements
data_integrity_requirements: Large dataset processing must maintain data accuracy
Performance must not compromise data integrity
System must handle maximum expected loads without failure
urs_requirements: URS-020-010: Load 100k data points in < 5 seconds on supported hardware
URS-020-011: Render charts in < 2 seconds after filter changes
related_tests: OQ-001: CSV Import and X-bar/R Chart Creation

test_cases.objective: Verify that users can successfully annotate data points on control charts with comments using the vendor's built-in annotation features.
prerequisites: System installed and configured
Valid user account with annotation permissions
Sample dataset loaded into the system
Control chart created from sample data

test_steps.action: Navigate to an existing X-bar/R chart displaying sample QC data points.
test_steps.expected_result: Chart loads successfully and displays all data points clearly.

test_steps.action: Select a specific data point on the chart and right-click to access the annotation menu.
test_steps.expected_result: Context menu appears with an 'Add Comment' or 'Annotate' option.

test_steps.action: Enter a test comment describing the data point and save the annotation.
test_steps.expected_result: Comment is saved and a visual indicator (e.g., icon) appears on the chart marking the annotated point.

test_steps.action: Hover over or click the annotated point to view the stored comment.
test_steps.expected_result: The previously entered comment is displayed in a tooltip or pop-up window.

test_steps.action: Export the chart to PDF using the standard export function.
test_steps.expected_result: PDF export completes successfully and includes the visual annotation marker.

acceptance_criteria: Users can add comments to any data point on control charts
Annotations are visually indicated on the chart
Comments are retrievable and viewable after saving
Annotations are included in exported reports
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records if comments are stored
GMP requirements for data traceability and explanation of outliers
data_integrity_requirements: Annotation records must be securely stored and cannot be inadvertently deleted
Comment history should be maintained with the chart configuration

test_cases.test_name: Read-Only Access and Configuration Change Audit Trail Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that released datasets are set to read-only and that configuration changes (if supported) are captured in the audit trail.
prerequisites: System installed with AD integration configured
User accounts with different privilege levels (Admin, User, Viewer)
Sample dataset marked as 'released' in the system

test_steps.action: Log in with a standard 'Viewer' role account and attempt to access a released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: User can view the dataset and charts but all edit/modify options are disabled or hidden.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of interface showing disabled controls

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify data points, chart parameters, or annotations on the released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents any modifications and displays a message indicating the dataset is read-only.

test_steps.action: Log in with an 'Admin' account and modify a chart configuration (e.g., change control limits) for a non-released dataset.
test_steps.expected_result: Changes are saved successfully if vendor supports configuration editing.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of configuration before and after change

test_steps.action: Access the system's audit trail log (if provided by vendor) and locate the record of the configuration change.
test_steps.expected_result: Audit trail entry shows the change made, timestamp, and user who made the modification.

test_steps.action: Verify that chart configurations themselves are saved as controlled records within the system.
test_steps.expected_result: System maintains version history or immutable records of chart configurations.

acceptance_criteria: Released datasets are inaccessible for modification by standard users
System enforces read-only access controls effectively
Configuration changes are recorded in audit trail (if vendor provides)
Chart configurations are maintained as controlled records
regulatory_basis: FDA 21 CFR Part 11 for access controls and audit trails
EU Annex 11 for electronic data integrity
GMP requirements for data protection
data_integrity_requirements: Immutable records for released data
Secure access controls to prevent unauthorized changes
Audit trail must be tamper-evident if provided

test_cases.test_name: ODBC Data Source Integration and Import Verification
test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can successfully connect to and import data from a configured ODBC data source using the vendor's standard connectors.
prerequisites: OQ-001 has been executed successfully
SPC dashboard is installed and configured
A test database with a known schema and sample QC data is available
A valid ODBC data source name (DSN) is configured on the system

test_steps.action: Navigate to the data import section of the SPC dashboard and select the ODBC import option.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays the ODBC connection configuration dialog with fields for DSN, username, and password.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the ODBC connection dialog

test_steps.action: Enter the pre-configured DSN, valid credentials, and a simple SQL query to select sample QC data from the test database.
test_steps.expected_result: The system establishes a connection to the database and displays a preview of the data returned by the query.

test_steps.action: Map the imported database columns to the required fields for creating an X-bar/R chart (e.g., subgroup identifier, measurement value).
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the column mappings and allows the user to proceed to chart creation.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the completed column mapping screen

test_steps.action: Generate an X-bar/R chart from the ODBC-imported data and apply the standard Nelson rules.
test_steps.expected_result: The system successfully generates a control chart displaying the data from the ODBC source, with Nelson rules applied correctly.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the final generated chart
Confirmation that Nelson rules are active

acceptance_criteria: The system successfully connects to the ODBC data source without errors.
Data is accurately imported and mapped from the external database.
A control chart is generated correctly from the ODBC-sourced data.
The functionality matches the vendor's documented standard behavior for ODBC connectors.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 for electronic records sourced from external systems
GAMP 5 for verification of configurable commercial software integration points
data_integrity_requirements: Data imported via ODBC must maintain accuracy and integrity from source to visualization.
The system shall not alter the original data values during the import process.
urs_requirements: URS-020-012: Import data from CSV and ODBC connections using standard connectors.
related_tests: OQ-001: CSV Import and X-bar/R Chart Creation with Nelson Rules

test_cases.objective: To verify that the SPC dashboard can integrate with Active Directory for user authentication, if this feature is supported by the vendor.
prerequisites: SPC dashboard is installed and configured
A test Active Directory environment is available
Vendor documentation confirms AD integration support
Test AD user accounts with different roles (e.g., Viewer, Analyst) are created

test_steps.action: Access the SPC dashboard's administrative settings and navigate to the authentication configuration section.
test_steps.expected_result: The system displays configuration options for authentication, including an option for Active Directory integration.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the authentication configuration screen

test_steps.action: Configure the connection to the test Active Directory by entering the required server details and domain information.
test_steps.expected_result: The system accepts the AD configuration and indicates a successful connection test to the directory.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the successful connection message

test_steps.action: Log out of the administrative account and attempt to log in using the credentials of a test AD user with 'Viewer' role permissions.
test_steps.expected_result: The system authenticates the user against AD and logs them in, presenting the dashboard interface restricted to the 'Viewer' role view.
data_to_capture: Screenshot of the post-login dashboard view

test_steps.action: Verify that the user's role-based permissions (e.g., read-only access to released datasets) are enforced correctly.
test_steps.expected_result: The user can only access views and functions permitted for the 'Viewer' role, as defined in URS-020-004 and URS-020-007.
data_to_capture: Screenshot demonstrating attempted unauthorized action is blocked

acceptance_criteria: The system can be configured to use Active Directory for authentication.
Users can successfully log in using their AD credentials.
Role-based access control is correctly mapped from AD groups or attributes.
The functionality operates as per the vendor's standard supported feature set.
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 §11.10(d) for secure, role-based access controls
GAMP 5 for testing configurable security features of commercial software
data_integrity_requirements: Authentication must be secure and prevent unauthorized access to the system and its data.
urs_requirements: URS-020-004: The dashboard shall allow role-based view access.
URS-020-007: Read-only access for released datasets.
URS-020-013: Integrate with AD for user authentication if supported by vendor.
related_tests: OQ-002: Role-Based Access Control and Export Functionality Verification

test_cases.test_name: Chart Configuration Retention and Controlled Records Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that chart configurations are properly retained as controlled records and cannot be modified after release
prerequisites: System installed and configured
User with configuration permissions logged in
Sample dataset loaded
Chart configuration created and saved

test_steps.action: Create a new chart configuration with specific parameters (control limits, rules, display settings)
test_steps.expected_result: Configuration is successfully created and saved in the system

test_steps.action: Mark the configuration as 'released' using the vendor's release workflow
test_steps.expected_result: Configuration status changes to released/controlled state

test_steps.action: Attempt to modify the released configuration parameters
test_steps.expected_result: System prevents modifications and displays read-only access message

test_steps.action: Verify configuration remains unchanged after system restart
test_steps.expected_result: Released configuration persists unchanged after system restart

acceptance_criteria: Released configurations cannot be modified
Configuration integrity maintained after system restart
Audit trail captures release actions if vendor provides this feature
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - Controlled records requirements
GMP requirements for configuration management
data_integrity_requirements: Configuration records must be immutable after release
System must maintain configuration version control
Integrity of statistical calculations must be preserved

test_cases.test_name: Multi-User Concurrent Access and Session Management Verification
test_cases.objective: Verify that multiple users can access the system concurrently without data corruption or session conflicts
prerequisites: System installed and configured
Multiple user accounts with different roles created
Network connectivity established
Sample datasets available

test_steps.action: Log in with two different user accounts simultaneously from separate workstations
test_steps.expected_result: Both users successfully authenticate and access the dashboard

test_steps.action: Have both users create different chart configurations simultaneously
test_steps.expected_result: Both configurations are saved independently without conflicts

test_steps.action: Have users access the same dataset concurrently for analysis
test_steps.expected_result: Both users can view and analyze the same data without locking issues
data_to_capture: Any data locking or contention issues

test_steps.action: Verify session timeout and re-authentication functionality
test_steps.expected_result: Sessions timeout appropriately and require re-authentication

acceptance_criteria: Multiple concurrent users can access system without conflicts
Session management functions correctly
Data integrity maintained during concurrent access
Role-based permissions enforced for all users
regulatory_basis: 21 CFR Part 11 - System access controls
GMP requirements for multi-user systems
data_integrity_requirements: Concurrent access must not corrupt data
User sessions must be properly isolated
Audit trails must correctly attribute actions to individual users
